SectionObject.Title: Max. depth, 100-year rain event, current situation
SectionObject.Text1:
A 100-year rain event is an extreme cloudburst that statistically occurs once every 100 years.

However, you don’t know when it will occur.
SectionObject.Text2: This data set shows estimated maximum water depth for the current situation.

SectionObject.Title: Estimated duration (>0.2 m), current situation
SectionObject.Text1:
A 100-year rain event is an extreme cloudburst that statistically occurs once every 100 years.

SectionObject.Text2: This data set shows how long water deeper than 0.2 m is expected to remain on the ground based on the current situation.

SectionObject.Title: Changed maximum water depth
SectionObject.Text1:
A 100-year rain event is an extreme cloudburst that statistically occurs once every 100 years.

However, you don’t know when it will occur.
SectionObject.Text2: This data set shows the effect of the infrastructure plan on maximum water depth with action taken. A negative depth (blue colour) means that the water depth has reduced as a result of the action taken, while a positive depth (red colour) means that the water depth has increased.
